articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026. This action continues the U.S. government's efforts to target entities and individuals supporting the Iranian regime.

Details of the specific entities and individuals designated were not immediately released in the initial announcement but are expected to be published in the Federal Register. These designations typically involve blocking property and interests in property of the designated persons subject to U.S. jurisdiction, and generally prohibiting U.S. persons from engaging in transactions with them.
These measures are part of a broader strategy to exert economic pressure on Iran, particularly in response to its nuclear program, support for regional proxy groups, and human rights abuses.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Imposes New Cuba Sanctions
body: On November 5, 2026, OFAC announced new designations targeting cyber-related and transnational criminal organizations, alongside new sanctions against Cuba. The action also included the publication of a Cuba-related determination.

The Cuba sanctions specifically target an offshore oil-shipping network, state-linked businesses, and Chinese suppliers to the Cuban military. Eight entities, two individuals, and five oil-carrying vessels were designated.

Additionally, the Treasury Department issued a determination under Executive Order 14404, authorizing sanctions against foreign persons operating in Cuba's electronics, manufacturing, marine, and technology sectors, effective November 5.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Updates Listings, and Amends Venezuela General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and updates to certain Iran-related listings on November 4, 2026. This action also included the publication of an Iran-related OFAC Alert.

Concurrently, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question. This amended General License 5AA further delays the effectiveness of the authorization in GL 5 until December 18, 2026, impacting transactions involving the PDVSA 2020 8.5% bond.

During the period between October 24, 2019, and December 18, 2026, transactions related to the sale or transfer of CITGO shares in connection with the PDVSA 2020 8.5% bond are prohibited unless specifically authorized by OFAC.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Iran-Related General License
body: On October 29, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Iran-related General License. This amendment modifies existing authorizations concerning transactions with Iran.

General Licenses are issued by OFAC to authorize activities that would otherwise be prohibited under sanctions programs. The specific details of the amendments were not immediately available but typically aim to clarify or adjust the scope of permitted activities.

Such amendments are often made in response to evolving policy considerations or to address practical implementation challenges faced by businesses and individuals operating under the sanctions regime.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entity for DPRK IT Worker Schemes; DRC Sanctions Imposed
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations on October 28, 2026, targeting 10 individuals and one entity involved in Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) government-run information technology (IT) worker schemes.
These schemes are accused of defrauding U.S. businesses and generating revenue for the DPRK's unlawful weapons of mass destruction (WMD) and ballistic missile programs.

Additionally, OFAC imposed new designations related to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). These actions are part of ongoing efforts to disrupt illicit financial activities and support for destabilizing actors globally.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Reporting
body: On October 26, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.

These amendments aim to provide updated guidance and clarification for U.S. persons on their obligations under OFAC sanctions programs. The FAQs are a critical resource for financial institutions and other entities to ensure compliance.
The revisions likely address common compliance challenges or reflect changes in OFAC's enforcement priorities and interpretations of existing regulations.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran and Russia General Licenses, Amends FAQs, and Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses on October 21, 2026. Concurrently, OFAC issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) to provide further guidance.

In addition to these new authorizations, OFAC also announced the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea. These removals indicate a reassessment of the sanctioned entities or a change in their activities.

The issuance of new General Licenses and the amendment of FAQs are part of OFAC's ongoing efforts to adapt its sanctions programs to evolving geopolitical landscapes and to provide clarity to the public on compliance requirements.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements PAIPA Designations and Issues Associated General Licenses
body: On October 19, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA). These designations are aimed at safeguarding American intellectual property.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC also issued associated General Licenses. These licenses typically authorize certain transactions or activities that would otherwise be prohibited under the PAIPA sanctions program, providing carve-outs for specific types of engagements.
The PAIPA designations underscore the U.S. government's commitment to combating intellectual property theft and protecting American innovation on a global scale.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License and FAQ
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question on October 16, 2026.

This action modifies existing guidance for transactions related to Venezuela. General Licenses are crucial for navigating the complex Venezuelan sanctions regime, allowing for specific, otherwise prohibited, activities.
The amendment likely provides further clarity or adjustments to the scope of permitted transactions, reflecting ongoing policy considerations regarding the situation in Venezuela.

Houthi officials reported on Saturday that airstrikes hit the village of al-Shariya in the Bani Hushaysh district, killing at least 27 people and wounding 30 others.

Polish police confirmed on Monday, November 9, that the shooter died in the hospital.
Polish Defense Minister Władysław Marcin Kosiniak-Kamysz described the tragedy as an 'act of terror,' and Poland has begun two days of national mourning.

articles.headline: UN Climate Summit COP31 Kicks Off in Turkey Amid Warnings of Accelerating Earth Heating
body: The annual UN climate conference, COP31, commenced in Antalya, Turkey, on November 9, 2026, with a stark warning from the UN's weather agency that Earth is accumulating heat at an accelerating rate.

The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) reported in its 'State of the Global Climate' update that the imbalance between incoming solar energy and outgoing energy from Earth reached its highest level since monitoring began.
The average surface temperature for January to September 2026 was approximately 1.47°C above the preindustrial average, with 2026 on track to be one of the four warmest years on record.

articles.headline: BIS Streamlines Export Controls for Sound Suppressors
body: The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced that, as of November 20, 2026, the export of certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors will be subject to BIS's Export Administration Regulations (EAR), rather than the State Department's U.S. Munitions List.

This deregulatory action aligns export controls on suppressors with those already applied to firearms, aiming to alleviate compliance burdens on the firearms industry while maintaining national security.

Under this new rule, suppressors will be added to the Commerce Control List (CCL), and BIS will require a license for certain exports, reexports, or in-country transfers, including releases of related software and technology to foreign persons.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: OCC Imposes $750 Million Assessment Against Bank of America for Deficient BSA/AML Compliance
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today announced a $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, N.A. (bank), for violations of the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations, including 12 CFR 21.21 and 12 CFR 21.11. This amount is the largest in OCC history.
